name: Dampen missile fire
summary: While the unit stands still, a wide, always-on field around it hampers every enemy rocket and missile weapon inside it: those launchers, on units and defences alike, fire much more slowly, while guns, shells and other weapons are untouched. It stops no shot outright; it blunts rocket-heavy attacks, so allies near the unit take far less of that fire. Moving switches it off. A deflect version makes missiles in the field veer off and miss instead, though strays still explode where they land. Unlike fire-countermeasures, it is passive and covers allies, not a self-only release on a key; unlike leave-hazard-zone, nothing is laid on the ground and it hampers one kind of weapon only; unlike the interceptor armour model, it shoots nothing down.
counterplay: Bring guns, cannons or artillery: shells and bullets ignore the field entirely.
Force the unit to move, by pressure or by flanking it: the field drops while it is on the move.
Fire missiles from outside the field's edge at targets outside it, or kill the field unit first with weapons it does not affect.
Disable or destroy the source; it is usually a support unit or device that needs an escort.

other_examples.note: The GDF's infantry specialist carries the same perk as the Shieldmaiden, with a smaller field: any enemy unit or building inside it whose attack is of the Rocket type fires at half its usual rate. The infantry version shows the pattern on a soldier, not only on a vehicle.

other_examples.note: A late GDF defence turret with a rocket battery that silences and marks what it hits; it also carries the interference field, as wide as the Shieldmaiden's, which passively slows the attacks of nearby enemy missile units. Its codex entry says it uses the same targeting jammer as the Shieldmaiden to help hold positions against missile bombardment.

other_examples.unit: ECM Tank (Zero Hour, China): missile jammer
other_examples.note: This unarmed support vehicle carries a passive jammer that makes guided missiles and rockets in a small radius around it go off course and miss, protecting a tank column or base defences from rocket attack. The strays are still live and can hit nearby units, shells are not affected, and the jammer goes off while the tank uses its vehicle-disabling beam. It cannot fight back against aircraft and needs an escort. The deflect variant of the pattern.

sources.title: ECM tank, Command & Conquer Wiki (Fandom)
sources.note: Its background section paraphrases the Zero Hour manual. Read from the shared page cache (copy fetched 2026-11-10).

shooter_analogues.note: In this top-down action game, the item's passive aura slows the attack speed (and healing) of every enemy within a wide radius of its carrier, always on; several carriers' auras do not stack, and the slow lingers briefly after an enemy leaves. It works best against enemies who already attack slowly. An always-on attack-slow field on a player character, though it slows every attack rather than one weapon type.

player_translation.summary: A support unit that plants itself and throws a wide jamming field around it: enemy rocket and missile launchers inside fire much more slowly, so the team holding that ground can shrug off rocket-heavy attackers. Moving switches the field off.
as_user: Stop beside the team's hold point or a vehicle push and the field comes up by itself; there is no key to press.
You read the enemy line-up: against rocket troops, missile vehicles and launcher defences you blunt their main damage; against guns and cannons you do nothing, so you pick your fights.
Every time you move to stay alive the field drops, so you choose between safety and protection.
Plant near enemy missile defences while your team assaults them, and their fire slows to a trickle.
as_target: Your rocket or missile weapon's fire rate visibly drops and an interference icon shows on your HUD while you are inside the field.
Back out of the field before you fire, or switch to a gun; against the deflect version, pick targets whose missile path stays clear of the field.
Push the field unit to make it move, or kill it with weapons it does not affect.
teammates: Protector: allies holding ground inside the field take much less rocket and missile fire.
Escort dependency: the field unit stands still and is usually lightly armed, so it needs teammates to keep enemies off it.
Counter-pick: the enemy team has to bring guns or artillery instead of rockets once a field unit shows up.
controls: No key: the field is passive and comes up whenever the unit has stood still for a moment, so it spends none of the tier's key budget.
Optional variant key (Q): toggle the field off to move without the warm-up, or switch to the deflect mode.
feedback: From above, a faint shimmering ring at the field's edge, team-coloured for allies and red for enemies, visible only while it is up.
Enemy rocket weapons inside show a stuttering muzzle and an interference icon; their HUD shows the slower fire rate.
A low electronic whine while the field runs that cuts out when the unit moves.
Deflect variant: missiles inside visibly wobble and veer off course.
changes_from_rts: Tempest Rising's field works on every enemy unit and defence with a Rocket-type weapon; a shooter needs every weapon tagged clearly as missile or rocket so players know which of their guns the field slows.
In the RTS the field is wide enough to cover a base; for a team shooter keep it to a squad-sized area, or it removes rocket units from whole fights.
The player must see when the field is up; the wiki pages describe nothing beyond the debuff icon, so a clear ring and a warm-up after stopping are proposed.
Generals' deflect version lets stray missiles land elsewhere; for players that randomness should be readable (missiles visibly veer) and fair.

team_play.notes: The field protects the teammates around it, not the carrier alone, and its value depends on the enemy bringing rockets; the stationary carrier needs an escort, and the enemy must answer by changing weapons or forcing it to move.

notes: Needs a weapon tag for rockets and missiles and a fire-rate modifier applied on the server to every enemy weapon with that tag inside a radius.
A still-for-a-moment test to raise and drop the field, with a short warm-up so it does not flicker.
Rules for overlap: several fields do not stack (as with Shiva's Guard), and defences are affected like units.
The deflect variant needs missile steering noise and stray-impact handling.
Against a rocket-heavy faction it can hard-counter whole units; keep the slow partial and the field squad-sized.
Several carriers at once must not stack, or rocket weapons become useless in that area.
Against gun-heavy enemies it does nothing, so the carrier needs another job (Tempest Rising's Shieldmaiden is an anti-air unit with a repair device).
A slower fire rate is easy to miss; the victim must see an interference icon and a visible edge to know why their launcher stutters.
Players must know which of their weapons count as rockets or missiles.

variants.name: Still field
variants.summary: The base form: a wide field around the unit, up only while it stands still, slows the fire of enemy rocket and missile weapons inside it.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Shieldmaiden, Missile Interference Aura (the Comms Officer and Haywire Turret carry the same perk; no stand-still condition is given for them)

variants.name: Moving field
variants.summary: The field stays up while the unit moves, so it escorts a push, but it is smaller.
variants.seen_in: Generals Zero Hour ECM Tank (the passive jammer works around the moving tank)

variants.name: Deflect missiles
variants.summary: Missiles and rockets inside the field veer off and miss instead of firing slower; the strays still explode where they land, and the field is off while the unit uses its other main tool.

variants.name: Fixed jammer
variants.summary: On a key, set down a destructible jamming device that carries the field on its own for a while.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Haywire Turret (a defence with the same field)

adds_weaknesses.why: The device stays where it was set and can be shot, so the enemy can destroy it or fight outside its reach.

variants.name: Slow all attacks
variants.summary: The field slows the attack rate of every enemy inside it, not only rocket and missile weapons, but it is smaller and does not stack.

adds_strengths.why: Enemy rocket and missile weapons near it fire much more slowly, so it and nearby allies shrug off rocket-heavy attacks and missile defences.

adds_weaknesses.why: Works only while standing still and does nothing against guns and shells, so pressure that makes it move, or a gun-armed enemy, takes it out of the fight.

counters.why: Rocket weapons inside the field fire at half rate in Tempest Rising, and the Generals ECM Tank is named as protection from rocket buggies.
Missile launchers inside the field fire slower (Tempest Rising) or are thrown off target (Generals ECM Tank).

countered_by.why: Shells are not affected by the Generals ECM Tank's jammer, and Tempest Rising's field touches only Rocket weapons.
Reasoned: Tempest Rising's field slows only Rocket-type weapons, so cannon-armed units fight at full rate inside it.

open_questions: Should the pattern stay limited to rockets and missiles, or widen to any one enemy weapon kind (the fill agent's wording, dampen-enemy-fire-aura), with rockets and missiles as the default? (Recommended: keep missiles as the base and the all-attacks version as a spicy variant.)
Should a field that only works while still need a short warm-up after stopping, so it cannot flicker on between steps?
Should the deflect variant's stray missiles be able to hit the field unit's own allies, as the Generals page says they can hit nearby units?
Tempest Rising counts Comms Officer and Haywire Turret carriers too; should a fixed defence version be a separate structure pattern later?

Two look-alikes were left out of this pattern: a timed shield projected around a unit that trims ranged hits on allies (the StarCraft II Sentry's Guardian Shield) belongs to raise-shield, and a placed device that shoots down grenades and missiles about to land near it (Apex Legends' Wattson pylon) intercepts rather than slows. Where should that interception device go: a deploy-turret variant or a pattern of its own?

shooter_fit.reason: An always-on support field is simple to play and creates clear escort and counter-pick choices, but a slower enemy fire rate is subtle to read from above and only matters when the enemy brings rockets, so it needs strong feedback.
